Profinite Borel completeness and smooth Artin motives

GrokRxiv review of arXiv:2606.25943 · math.AT

Yorick Fuhrmann

TL;DR

The five specialist reviewers converge on a picture of a mathematically significant but reproducibility-deficient paper. The novelty reviewer rates the contribution as significant (0.75), crediting a genuine generalization of Voevodsky's field-level equivalence of Artin motives with permutation modules to arbitrary connected noetherian schemes of finite Krull dimension, and an extension of Borel completeness theory from finite to profinite groups with a conceptually precise two-notion framework (levelwise vs. hypercomplete). The summary and citation reviews corroborate the paper's technical ambition and mostly strong bibliographic practice. The tension in the specialist panel is between the technical correctness reviewer (confidence 0.58, overall 'mostly_sound') and the reproducibility reviewer (confidence 0.86, score 0.22): both flag the same gap — Theorems 1, 2, and 3, the three headline results, carry no machine-checkable proof artifacts, with the technical reviewer rating all three as 'unsupported' at major severity and the reproducibility reviewer rating the corresponding absences at critical severity. Per the recommendation gate for a paper in the math.* (code-amenable) field where both technical_correctness and reproducibility independently flagged major or critical missing proof-as-code artifacts for the headline claims, the default is major_revision. The missing artifacts do not indicate the proofs are incorrect — the technical reviewer calls the arguments 'mathematically sound' and 'internally consistent and plausible' — but load-bearing steps (the pushforward-degree identity in Theorem 1, the acyclic-orthogonality argument in Theorem 2, full commutativity of the 3×3 diagram in Theorem 3) remain unverified by any formal or computational check. One subsidiary issue is the disclosed non-hypercomplete étale gap (C10, minor): one cell of Theorem 3 is explicitly deferred with no machine-verifiable treatment. Citation practice is strong; the one flagged concern (bcn25 cited for a Mackey functor example in a PD-operads paper) warrants author verification but is plausibly a citation-key collision rather than an error in reasoning.

Recommendation: Major revision · Confidence: 72%

Strengths

  • The profinite Borel completeness theory is a technically demanding and conceptually clean generalization of Mathew–Naumann–Noel's finite-group results: two distinct notions are introduced (levelwise and hypercomplete Borel completeness), their relationship via hypercompletion is made precise, and conditions for coincidence (finite virtual cohomological dimension, per Clausen–Mathew) are correctly identified.
  • Theorem 1 extends Voevodsky's classical equivalence of smooth Artin motives with permutation G-modules from fields to arbitrary connected noetherian schemes of finite Krull dimension, using the étale fundamental group as the profinite group; this is a genuine and non-trivial advance over Balmer–Gallauer's field-level framework.
  • The commutative 3×3 diagram of Theorem 3 unifies derived permutation modules, equivariant module spectra, Borel and levelwise-Borel complete categories, and Nisnevich/étale/hyper-étale sheaves with transfers into a single coherent structural picture, providing substantial organizational and computational leverage.
  • Citation hygiene across 147 references is strong and reflects thorough engagement with foundational literature in equivariant homotopy theory, motivic cohomology, and ∞-category theory; the most heavily cited foundational sources (Barwick, Barwick–Glasman–Shah, Balmer–Gallauer, Cisinski–Déglise, Clausen–Mathew) are credited appropriately and their results are applied with evident familiarity.
  • The paper transparently discloses the one remaining gap (the non-hypercomplete étale row of the motivic diagram), correctly identifies what computation is needed to close it, and does not overstate what is established.

Weaknesses

  • Theorems 1, 2, and 3 — the three headline results — each lack machine-checkable proof artifacts: the load-bearing pushforward-degree identity and cohomological-ideal vanishing in Theorem 1 (C1, major), the acyclic-orthogonality hypercompletion argument in Theorem 2 (C2, major), and the full square-by-square commutativity of the 3×3 diagram in Theorem 3 (C3, major) are presented as human proofs only; in a code-amenable math.* field this leaves the central claims formally unverified.
  • Reproducibility infrastructure is absent: no public repository, no formal proof environment specification, no proof-check commands, and no dependency lockfile are provided, yielding a reproducibility score of 0.22; all three main theorem gaps are rated critical severity by the reproducibility reviewer.
  • The non-hypercomplete étale row of Theorem 3's diagram — the identification of a third row with DAM_ét(S;R) — is explicitly deferred because the required mapping-space computation in effective motives was not carried out, leaving one cell of the main structural theorem unestablished (C10, minor).
  • Citation entry bcn25 (Brantner–Campos–Nuiten, 'PD operads and explicit partition Lie algebras') is cited for a spectral Mackey functor description (Example 2.15), a topically unexpected use that may reflect a citation-key collision; the mismatch between the paper's primary subject and its cited function warrants author verification.
  • The literature review does not address any ∞-categorical treatments of profinite group actions on spectra in the 2008–2024 window between Fausk and bbb24, nor does it explicitly assert the absence of such work; the related-work picture for the profinite equivariant homotopy theory part of the paper is therefore incomplete.
  • Review-loop policy blocker: Review-loop bundle completeness failed: declared artifact `review_loop/lean/env/env_result.json` is missing and has no skip_reason

Open Questions

  • Can the authors provide machine-checkable proof artifacts (Lean, Agda, or equivalent) for the load-bearing steps identified in C1–C3 — specifically the pushforward-degree identity and cohomological-ideal vanishing (Theorem 1), the acyclic-orthogonality argument (Theorem 2), and square-by-square commutativity (Theorem 3) — or supply a detailed justification for why formalization is not feasible for this work?
  • Is the citation to bcn25 (Brantner–Campos–Nuiten, 'PD operads and explicit partition Lie algebras') for Example 2.15 in the spectral Mackey functor description intended, and if so, can the authors confirm that the cited example content appears in that paper? If not, which citation key was intended?
  • What is the status of the mapping-space computation needed to establish the non-hypercomplete étale row DAM_ét(S;R) in Theorem 3's diagram — is this result expected to appear in a companion paper, and if so, can a more precise statement of the open problem and its expected difficulty be added?
  • The t-structure on $Sp^G_lwBorel$ (Proposition 6) is load-bearing for Theorem 2 via the acyclic-orthogonality argument; can the authors make the verification of t-structure axioms and right-completeness fully explicit in the proof, or provide a pointer to the precise location in the text where these are verified?
  • Are there ∞-categorical treatments of profinite group actions on spectra from the period 2008–2024 (between Fausk and bbb24) that the authors considered and chose not to cite, or does the literature genuinely contain no intervening accounts that would bear on the paper's profinite Borel completeness theory?

  "summary": "The paper's citation hygiene is overall strong: 147 references reflect thorough engagement with equivariant homotopy theory, motivic cohomology, and ∞-category theory, and the bibliography consistently credits foundational sources alongside recent companion papers by Balmer–Gallauer, Barwick, Clausen–Mathew, and Cisinski–Déglise. One entry warrants scrutiny: bcn25 (Brantner–Campos–Nuiten, 'PD operads and explicit partition Lie algebras') is cited for a spectral Mackey functor description (Example 2.15), a topically unexpected use that may reflect a citation-key error or an incidental example in an otherwise unrelated paper. The bgv25 entry records 'published online first' as a volume field, a minor bibliographic imprecision. Only 32 of 147 entries were available for review; the most heavily cited references (Lurie HTT/HA/SAG, Mathew–Naumann–Noel, Clausen–Mathew, Cisinski–Déglise, SGA1, Voevodsky) fall in the omitted 115 and could not be assessed."

      "text": "The t-structure on Sp^G_lwBorel (Proposition 6) is load-bearing for Theorem 2 via the acyclic-orthogonality argument; can the authors make the verification of t-structure axioms and right-completeness fully explicit in the proof, or provide a pointer to the precise location in the text where these are verified?",
      "verifier_status": "pass"
    },
    {
      "id": "claim_30",
      "role": "meta_reviewer",
      "text": "Are there ∞-categorical treatments of profinite group actions on spectra from the period 2008–2024 (between Fausk and bbb24) that the authors considered and chose not to cite, or does the literature genuinely contain no intervening accounts that would bear on the paper's profinite Borel completeness theory?",
      "verifier_status": "pass"
    },
    {
      "id": "claim_31",
      "role": "novelty",
      "text": "significant",
      "verifier_status": "pass"
    },
    {
      "id": "claim_32",
      "role": "novelty",
      "text": "builds_on",
      "verifier_status": "pass"
    },
    {
      "id": "claim_33",
      "role": "novelty",
      "text": "This paper extends MNN's Borel completeness theory from finite groups to profinite groups. It adds a coefficients version throughout, introduces two new notions (levelwise Borel completeness and its hypercompletion), and identifies the latter with full Borel completeness — results that have no analogue in MNN for finite groups.",
      "verifier_status": "pass"
    },
    {
      "id": "claim_34",
      "role": "novelty",
      "text": "builds_on",
      "verifier_status": "pass"
    },
    {
      "id": "claim_35",
      "role": "novelty",
      "text": "Voevodsky identified Artin motives over a field with permutation modules for the absolute Galois group. This paper extends that equivalence to arbitrary connected noetherian schemes of finite Krull dimension, replacing the Galois group by the profinite étale fundamental group and using the new profinite Borel completeness machinery to do so.",
      "verifier_status": "pass"
    },
    {
      "id": "claim_36",
      "role": "novelty",
      "text": "builds_on",
      "verifier_status": "pass"
    },
    {
      "id": "claim_37",
      "role": "novelty",
      "text": "Balmer–Gallauer revisited Voevodsky's field-level equivalence using derived permutation modules. This paper uses their framework as the target of the extended equivalence over general base schemes and draws on their category D-Perm(G;R) as the algebraic avatar of smooth Artin motives.",
      "verifier_status": "pass"
    },
    {
      "id": "claim_38",
      "role": "novelty",
      "text": "builds_on",
      "verifier_status": "pass"
    },
    {
      "id": "claim_39",
      "role": "novelty",
      "text": "Cisinski–Déglise's theorem that étale sheaves on finite étale schemes automatically have transfers is used as a key input. The paper gives an independent equivariant proof of this result and uses their six-functor formalism to handle the étale/hypercomplete distinction in motives.",
      "verifier_status": "pass"
    },
    {
      "id": "claim_40",
      "role": "novelty",
      "text": "builds_on",
      "verifier_status": "pass"
    },
    {
      "id": "claim_41",
      "role": "novelty",
      "text": "Provides the theory of finite correspondences with coefficients used to define Voevodsky motives over a general base scheme S with R-coefficients, which is essential for formulating the main motivic theorem.",
      "verifier_status": "pass"
    },
    {
      "id": "claim_42",
      "role": "novelty",
      "text": "builds_on",
      "verifier_status": "pass"
    },
    {
      "id": "claim_43",
      "role": "novelty",
      "text": "Clausen–Mathew's result that both rows of the main commutative diagram agree when the virtual cohomological dimension of G is finite is invoked to give conditions under which levelwise and full Borel completeness coincide, collapsing the two distinct notions.",
      "verifier_status": "pass"
    },
    {
      "id": "claim_44",
      "role": "novelty",
      "text": "prior_art",
      "verifier_status": "pass"
    },
    {
      "id": "claim_45",
      "role": "novelty",
      "text": "Ayoub–Zucker study étale Artin motives over general bases without transfers. This paper handles the same setting with transfers, yielding a richer equivariant and representation-theoretic description not available in their approach.",
      "verifier_status": "pass"
    },
    {
      "id": "claim_46",
      "role": "novelty",
      "text": "competing",
      "verifier_status": "pass"
    },
    {
      "id": "claim_47",
      "role": "novelty",
      "text": "Ruimy studies integral étale Artin motives without transfers. This paper's approach using equivariant spectra with transfers provides a complementary and more structured description via Borel complete G-spectra, valid under the appropriate torsion/characteristic hypotheses.",
      "verifier_status": "pass"
    },
    {
      "id": "claim_48",
      "role": "novelty",
      "text": "orthogonal",
      "verifier_status": "pass"
    },
    {
      "id": "claim_49",
      "role": "novelty",
      "text": "Provides foundational models for Sp^G for profinite G and develops their tensor-triangular geometry. This paper uses those models as input but develops different structural results — levelwise vs. full Borel completeness and connections to motives — not addressed by Balchin–Barnes–Barthel.",
      "verifier_status": "pass"
    },
    {
      "id": "claim_50",
      "role": "novelty",
      "text": "builds_on",
      "verifier_status": "pass"
    },
    {
      "id": "claim_51",
      "role": "novelty",
      "text": "Fuhrmann's identification of D-Perm(G;R) with Mod_{underline{R}}(Sp^G) (modules over the Bredon cohomology spectrum) is cited as a key ingredient in the equivariant description of smooth Artin motives in the proof of the main theorem.",
      "verifier_status": "pass"
    },
    {
      "id": "claim_52",
      "role": "novelty",
      "text": "builds_on",
      "verifier_status": "pass"
    },
    {
      "id": "claim_53",
      "role": "novelty",
      "text": "Barnes–Taggart's colimit description of Sp^G for profinite G as a filtered colimit of Sp^{G_i} is used as the foundational recollection from which the levelwise Borel complete category is constructed.",
      "verifier_status": "pass"
    },
    {
      "id": "claim_54",
      "role": "summary",
      "text": "The paper develops a theory of Borel complete equivariant spectra for profinite groups and identifies smooth Artin motives over general base schemes with modules over Bredon cohomology spectra.",
      "verifier_status": "pass"
    },
    {
      "id": "claim_55",
      "role": "summary",
      "text": "This paper bridges equivariant homotopy theory and algebraic geometry by studying how certain categorical structures behave when controlled by infinite Galois groups. The main result shows that smooth Artin motives—geometric objects tracking finite étale covers of a scheme—can be understood as representations of the étale fundamental group, extending a classical theorem of Voevodsky from fields to arbitrary schemes.\n\nThe paper is organized in two parts. First, the authors develop the theory of …",
      "verifier_status": "pass"
    },
    {
      "id": "claim_56",
      "role": "summary",
      "text": "Extended Borel completeness theory from finite to profinite groups with coefficients, and identified two notions (levelwise and hypercomplete) with the hypercomplete objects forming the Borel complete category",
      "verifier_status": "pass"
    },
    {
      "id": "claim_57",
      "role": "summary",
      "text": "Defined smooth Artin motives over general base schemes with coefficients and proved they are equivalent to modules over Bredon cohomology spectra of the étale fundamental group",
      "verifier_status": "pass"
    },
    {
      "id": "claim_58",
      "role": "summary",
      "text": "Established a commutative diagram relating permutation modules, equivariant spectra, Borel complete spectra, representations, and étale sheaves with transfers",
      "verifier_status": "pass"
    },
    {
      "id": "claim_59",
      "role": "summary",
      "text": "Proved that étale smooth Artin motives admit descriptions in terms of Borel complete equivariant spectra, with the sheaf/hypersheaf distinction corresponding to levelwise/hypercomplete Borel completeness",
      "verifier_status": "pass"
    },
    {
      "id": "claim_60",
      "role": "technical_correctness",
      "text": "mostly_sound",
      "verifier_status": "pass"
    }
  ],

}

meta_reviewer — sonnet[1m] pass

The five specialist reviewers converge on a picture of a mathematically significant but reproducibility-deficient paper. The novelty reviewer rates the contribution as significant (0.75), crediting a genuine generalization of Voevodsky's field-level equivalence of Artin motives with permutation modules to arbitrary connected noetherian schemes of finite Krull dimension, and an extension of Borel completeness theory from finite to profinite groups with a conceptually precise two-notion framework (levelwise vs. hypercomplete). The summary and citation reviews corroborate the paper's technical ambition and mostly strong bibliographic practice. The tension in the specialist panel is between the technical correctness reviewer (confidence 0.58, overall 'mostly_sound') and the reproducibility reviewer (confidence 0.86, score 0.22): both flag the same gap — Theorems 1, 2, and 3, the three headline results, carry no machine-checkable proof artifacts, with the technical reviewer rating all three as 'unsupported' at major severity and the reproducibility reviewer rating the corresponding absences at critical severity. Per the recommendation gate for a paper in the math.* (code-amenable) field where both technical_correctness and reproducibility independently flagged major or critical missing proof-as-code artifacts for the headline claims, the default is major_revision. The missing artifacts do not indicate the proofs are incorrect — the technical reviewer calls the arguments 'mathematically sound' and 'internally consistent and plausible' — but load-bearing steps (the pushforward-degree identity in Theorem 1, the acyclic-orthogonality argument in Theorem 2, full commutativity of the 3×3 diagram in Theorem 3) remain unverified by any formal or computational check. One subsidiary issue is the disclosed non-hypercomplete étale gap (C10, minor): one cell of Theorem 3 is explicitly deferred with no machine-verifiable treatment. Citation practice is strong; the one flagged concern (bcn25 cited for a Mackey functor example in a PD-operads paper) warrants author verification but is plausibly a citation-key collision rather than an error in reasoning.

Recommendation: Major revision · Confidence: 72%

Strengths

  • The profinite Borel completeness theory is a technically demanding and conceptually clean generalization of Mathew–Naumann–Noel's finite-group results: two distinct notions are introduced (levelwise and hypercomplete Borel completeness), their relationship via hypercompletion is made precise, and conditions for coincidence (finite virtual cohomological dimension, per Clausen–Mathew) are correctly identified.
  • Theorem 1 extends Voevodsky's classical equivalence of smooth Artin motives with permutation G-modules from fields to arbitrary connected noetherian schemes of finite Krull dimension, using the étale fundamental group as the profinite group; this is a genuine and non-trivial advance over Balmer–Gallauer's field-level framework.
  • The commutative 3×3 diagram of Theorem 3 unifies derived permutation modules, equivariant module spectra, Borel and levelwise-Borel complete categories, and Nisnevich/étale/hyper-étale sheaves with transfers into a single coherent structural picture, providing substantial organizational and computational leverage.
  • Citation hygiene across 147 references is strong and reflects thorough engagement with foundational literature in equivariant homotopy theory, motivic cohomology, and ∞-category theory; the most heavily cited foundational sources (Barwick, Barwick–Glasman–Shah, Balmer–Gallauer, Cisinski–Déglise, Clausen–Mathew) are credited appropriately and their results are applied with evident familiarity.
  • The paper transparently discloses the one remaining gap (the non-hypercomplete étale row of the motivic diagram), correctly identifies what computation is needed to close it, and does not overstate what is established.

Weaknesses

  • Theorems 1, 2, and 3 — the three headline results — each lack machine-checkable proof artifacts: the load-bearing pushforward-degree identity and cohomological-ideal vanishing in Theorem 1 (C1, major), the acyclic-orthogonality hypercompletion argument in Theorem 2 (C2, major), and the full square-by-square commutativity of the 3×3 diagram in Theorem 3 (C3, major) are presented as human proofs only; in a code-amenable math.* field this leaves the central claims formally unverified.
  • Reproducibility infrastructure is absent: no public repository, no formal proof environment specification, no proof-check commands, and no dependency lockfile are provided, yielding a reproducibility score of 0.22; all three main theorem gaps are rated critical severity by the reproducibility reviewer.
  • The non-hypercomplete étale row of Theorem 3's diagram — the identification of a third row with DAM_ét(S;R) — is explicitly deferred because the required mapping-space computation in effective motives was not carried out, leaving one cell of the main structural theorem unestablished (C10, minor).
  • Citation entry bcn25 (Brantner–Campos–Nuiten, 'PD operads and explicit partition Lie algebras') is cited for a spectral Mackey functor description (Example 2.15), a topically unexpected use that may reflect a citation-key collision; the mismatch between the paper's primary subject and its cited function warrants author verification.
  • The literature review does not address any ∞-categorical treatments of profinite group actions on spectra in the 2008–2024 window between Fausk and bbb24, nor does it explicitly assert the absence of such work; the related-work picture for the profinite equivariant homotopy theory part of the paper is therefore incomplete.

The argument reads as mathematically sound, but no machine-checkable artifact is shipped. The load-bearing pushforward-degree identity ((π^H̄_K̄)_*⟨X/K̄⟩ = [H:K]·⟨X/H̄⟩) and the vanishing of the cohomological ideal I(G) under Ψ are concrete, code-verifiable computations left unbacked by a formal proof or symbolic check.

  • Is the citation to bcn25 (Brantner–Campos–Nuiten, 'PD operads and explicit partition Lie algebras') for Example 2.15 in the spectral Mackey functor description intended, and if so, can the authors confirm that the cited example content appears in that paper? If not, which citation key was intended?
  • What is the status of the mapping-space computation needed to establish the non-hypercomplete étale row DAM_ét(S;R) in Theorem 3's diagram — is this result expected to appear in a companion paper, and if so, can a more precise statement of the open problem and its expected difficulty be added?
  • The t-structure on $Sp^G_lwBorel$ (Proposition 6) is load-bearing for Theorem 2 via the acyclic-orthogonality argument; can the authors make the verification of t-structure axioms and right-completeness fully explicit in the proof, or provide a pointer to the precise location in the text where these are verified?
  • Are there ∞-categorical treatments of profinite group actions on spectra from the period 2008–2024 (between Fausk and bbb24) that the authors considered and chose not to cite, or does the literature genuinely contain no intervening accounts that would bear on the paper's profinite Borel completeness theory?

        "body_markdown": "It is a classical result of Grothendieck [@sga1 §5, Théorème 4.1] that\nfinite étale schemes over a connected base scheme $S$ are nothing but\nfinite discrete sets with a continuous action of the étale fundamental\ngroup $\\pi_1^{\\textnormal{ét}}(S)$, in symbols $$\\begin{equation}\n\\label{eq:fetspione}\n\\textsf{\\textup{Fét}}_S\\simeq \\pi_1^{\\textnormal{ét}}(S)\\textsf{\\textup{-set}}.\n\\end{equation}$$ When $S$ is the spectrum of a field $\\mathbb{F}$ we can\nfollow Voevodsky's approach to motives and construct an additive\ncategory of *$\\mathbb{F}$-correspondences*\n$\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(\\mathbb{F};\\mathbb{Z})$ from the category of\nsmooth $\\mathbb{F}$-schemes $\\textsf{\\textup{Sm}}_\\mathbb{F}$. For a\ncommutative ring $R$, additive $R$-module valued presheaves on\n$\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(\\mathbb{F};\\mathbb{Z})$ which are sheaves for\nthe Nisnevich topology are called *sheaves with transfers*. From the\ncategory they comprise one constructs effective Voevodsky motives\n$\\mathcal{DM}_{\\textnormal{Nis}}^{\\textnormal{eff}}(\\mathbb{F};R)$\nthrough passage to the derived category followed by\n$\\mathbb{A}^1$-localisation, and there is an 'associated motive' functor\n$$\\mathcal{M}_\\textnormal{Nis}: \\; \\textsf{\\textup{Sm}}_\\mathbb{F}\\to \\mathcal{DM}_{\\textnormal{Nis}}^{\\textnormal{eff}}(\\mathbb{F};R).$$\nUnder this linearisation procedure *Artin motives*\n$\\mathcal{DAM}_{\\textnormal{Nis}}(\\mathbb{F};R)$, defined as the\nlocalising subcategory inside\n$\\mathcal{DM}_{\\textnormal{Nis}}^{\\textnormal{eff}}(\\mathbb{F};R)$\ngenerated by the motives associated to $0$-dimensional smooth\n$\\mathbb{F}$-schemes, are closely related to permutation representations\nof $\\textnormal{Gal}(\\mathbb{F}^{\\textnormal{sep}}/\\mathbb{F})$, the\nabsolute Galois group of the field $\\mathbb{F}$. This was originally\nobserved by Voevodsky [@voe00 §3.4] and has recently been revisited by\nBalmer--Gallauer [@bg23 §7]. Namely, there is a symmetric monoidal\nequivalence $$\\begin{equation}\n\\label{eq:damaspermfield}\n\\mathcal{DAM}_{\\textnormal{Nis}}(\\mathbb{F};R) \\simeq \\mathcal{D}\\textsf{\\textup{Perm}}(\\textnormal{Gal}(\\mathbb{F}^{\\textnormal{sep}}/\\mathbb{F});R),\n\\end{equation}$$ where the latter is the category of derived permutation\nmodules defined in [@bg22a]. Since the absolute Galois group\n$\\textnormal{Gal}(\\mathbb{F}^{\\textnormal{sep}}/\\mathbb{F})$ is\nprecisely the étale fundamental group of the scheme\n$\\textnormal{Spec}(\\mathbb{F})$, the equivalence\n[\\[eq:fetspione\\]](#eq:fetspione){reference-type=\"ref\"\nreference=\"eq:fetspione\"} suggests a natural question:\n\n::: center\n*Is [\\[eq:damaspermfield\\]](#eq:damaspermfield){reference-type=\"ref\"\nreference=\"eq:damaspermfield\"} still true when we replace\n$\\textnormal{Spec}(\\mathbb{F})$ by a general base scheme $S$\\\nand $\\textnormal{Gal}(\\mathbb{F}^{\\textnormal{sep}}/\\mathbb{F})$ by its\nétale fundamental group?*\n:::\n\nWe answer this question in the affirmative, under mild assumptions on\nthe base scheme. To this end, we define the $\\infty$-category of\neffective Voevodsky motives\n$$\\mathcal{DM}_{\\textnormal{Nis}}^{\\textnormal{eff}}(S;R) \\mathrel{\\vcenter{\\baselineskip 0.4ex \\lineskiplimit 0pt\n\\hbox{\\scriptsize.}\\hbox{\\scriptsize.}}}%\n=L_{\\mathbb{A}^1}\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\textnormal{Nis}}(\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$$\nover a base scheme $S$ with coefficients in $R$ as the $\\infty$-category\nof $\\mathbb{A}^1$-invariant Nisnevich sheaves with transfers with values\nin spectra.[^1] For this, we employ the theory of finite correspondences\nwith coefficients [@cd19 §9]. Voevodsky motives are usually defined by\nfirst deriving the $1$-category of Nisnevich sheaves with transfers. In\nAppendix [6](#sec:sheaveswithtransfers){reference-type=\"ref\"\nreference=\"sec:sheaveswithtransfers\"} we show that both of these\napproaches are equivalent.\\\nWe are then in a position to consider specific subcategories of motives,\nand we define the $\\infty$-category of *smooth Artin motives*\n$$\\mathcal{DAM}_\\textnormal{Nis}(S;R) \\mathrel{\\vcenter{\\baselineskip 0.4ex \\lineskiplimit 0pt\n\\hbox{\\scriptsize.}\\hbox{\\scriptsize.}}}%\n=\\textnormal{Loc}(\\mathcal{M}_{\\textnormal{Nis}}(X) \\mid X \\textnormal{ finite étale over } S)$$\nas the localising subcategory of\n$\\mathcal{DM}_\\textnormal{Nis}^{\\textnormal{eff}}(S;R)$ generated by the\nmotives associated to finite étale $S$-schemes. When $S$ is the spectrum\nof a field, this recovers the notion of Artin motives that was\nconsidered by Voevodsky. Crucially relying on the equivalence\n[\\[eq:fetspione\\]](#eq:fetspione){reference-type=\"ref\"\nreference=\"eq:fetspione\"}, we then show:\n\n::: thm*\n**Theorem 1** ([1](#thm:damnisasmodunderlr){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"thm:damnisasmodunderlr\"}). *Let $S$ be a connected,\nnoetherian scheme of finite Krull dimension. Then there is a symmetric\nmonoidal equivalence\n$$\\mathcal{DAM}_\\textnormal{Nis}(S;R) \\simeq \\mathcal{D}\\textsf{\\textup{Perm}}(\\pi_1^{\\textnormal{ét}}(S,s);R),$$\nwhere $s: \\textnormal{Spec}(k) \\to S$ is a geometric point of $S$.*\n:::\n\nThe $\\infty$-categories above are presentably symmetric monoidal stable\n$\\infty$-categories and hence their homotopy categories are 'large'\ntt-categories. By recent work of Balmer--Gallauer [@bg25a; @bg25b], the\nBalmer spectrum of the compact part of\n$\\mathcal{D}\\textsf{\\textup{Perm}}(G;R)$ (and hence of *geometric*\nsmooth Artin motives) is known for any profinite group $G$ when $R$ is a\nfield, and by work of Dubey--Gómez [@dg25] its set is known when $G$ is\nfinite and $R$ is Noetherian.\\\nIn fact, in order to prove the above theorem, we work with an\nequivariant description of the $\\infty$-category\n$\\mathcal{D}\\textsf{\\textup{Perm}}(\\pi_1^{\\textnormal{ét}}(S,s);R)$,\nwhich by Corollary 4.8 or Theorem 5.12 of [@fuh25] is given by\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{\\underline{R}}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)$, modules\nover the $R$-linear Bredon cohomology spectrum in equivariant spectra\nfor the profinite group $G=\\pi_1^{\\textnormal{ét}}(S,s)$. In the proof\nwe rely on its spectral Mackey functor description, see [@bcn25 Example\n2.15] or [@fuh25 Corollary 3.18].\\\nSo far we have used the Nisnevich topology for the motives we\nconsidered, but replacing it by the étale topology comes with no\ndifficulty, yielding étale versions\n$$\\mathcal{DM}_{\\textnormal{ét}}^{(\\wedge),\\textnormal{eff}}(S;R) \\mathrel{\\vcenter{\\baselineskip 0.4ex \\lineskiplimit 0pt\n\\hbox{\\scriptsize.}\\hbox{\\scriptsize.}}}%\n=L_{\\mathbb{A}^1}\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\textnormal{ét}}^{(\\wedge)}(\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$$\ninside which we can similarly define smooth Artin motives. As indicated\nby the superscript $(\\wedge)$, in the étale case it is crucial to\ndistinguish between sheaves and hypersheaves, since the étale topos of a\nscheme is generally not hypercomplete. For this we again use sheaves\nwith transfers - versions of Artin motives for the étale topology but\nwithout transfers have among others been considered by Ayoub--Zucker\n[@az12] and Ruimy [@rui25a; @rui25b]. It is now an easy observation that\nétale (hyper)sheafification on sheaves with transfers descends to\nmotives, and there is a second natural question:\n\n::: center\n*Do étale smooth Artin motives also admit descriptions in terms of\\\nrepresentation theory and equivariant homotopy theory?*\n:::\n\nTo answer this question, we will take a digression into equivariant\nhomotopy theory, which will take up the first two sections. Let us\noutline our considerations.\\\nWhen $G$ is a finite group, a $G$-spectrum $X$ is *Borel complete* if\nmaps $Y \\to X$ are null whenever $Y$ is nonequivariantly contractible,\ni.e. $\\textnormal{res}^G_1(Y) \\simeq 0$, or equivalently\n$Y \\otimes \\mathbb{D}(G) \\simeq 0$, where $\\mathbb{D}(G)$ is the\nequivariant function dual of the orbit $\\Sigma^{\\infty}_+G/1$. This\nalready suggests that in this case the 'genuine' $G$-action on $X$\nshould come from a 'naive' one, which is made precise by the\nidentification of the Borel complete subcategory of\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G$ as a functor category\n$$\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G_{\\textnormal{Borel}} \\simeq \\textnormal{Fun}(BG,\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$$\nestablished by Mathew--Naumann--Noel in [@mnn17 §6.3]. In terms of\nspectral Mackey functors [@bar17], we can think of Borel completion as\nan evaluation at the orbit $G/1$. If one tries to generalise these\nstatements to profinite groups, one faces the difficulty that the\nequivariant homotopy theory of such groups is already controlled by the\nfinite (discrete) $G$-sets, and the orbit $G/1$ is not among such.\\\nInstead, it is an easy observation that Borel complete equivariant\nspectra are preserved by categorical fixed points for arbitrary normal\nsubgroups. Since $G$-spectra for profinite $G=\\textnormal{lim}_i \\, G_i$\nare themselves a limit along categorical fixed points, we can define a\nfull subcategory\n$$\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G_{\\textnormal{lwBorel}} \\mathrel{\\vcenter{\\baselineskip 0.4ex \\lineskiplimit 0pt\n\\hbox{\\scriptsize.}\\hbox{\\scriptsize.}}}%\n=\\textnormal{lim}_i \\; \\textnormal{Spec}^{G_i}_{\\textnormal{Borel}} \\subseteq \\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G,$$\nthe objects of which we call *levelwise Borel complete*. We can view\nobjects of $\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G$ as families of $G_i$-spectra\n$(X_i)_{i \\in I}$ which are compatible with respect to categorical fixed\npoints, i.e. $X_i^{N_{ij}} \\simeq X_j$, where $N_{ij}$ is the kernel of\nthe canonical map $G_i \\twoheadrightarrow G_j$. Such an object is\nlevelwise Borel complete if each $X_i$ is a Borel complete\n$G_i$-spectrum.\\\nA second possible approach is motivated by the observation that in a\nprofinite group the trivial subgroup is the intersection of all open\nnormal subgroups. Instead of working with the dual $\\mathbb{D}(G)$ of\nthe orbit $\\Sigma^{\\infty}_+G/1$ as one does in the finite group case,\none should thus consider the duals $\\mathbb{D}(G/N_i)$ of all open\nnormal subgroups at the same time, where $N_i$ is the kernel of the\nnatural map $G \\twoheadrightarrow G_i$. They assemble into a filtered\ndiagram in $\\textnormal{CAlg}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)$, and we denote\nits colimit by\n$A \\mathrel{\\vcenter{\\baselineskip 0.4ex \\lineskiplimit 0pt\n\\hbox{\\scriptsize.}\\hbox{\\scriptsize.}}}%\n=\\textnormal{colim}_i \\, \\mathbb{D}(G/N_i)$. It naturally identifies\nwith $\\textnormal{coind}^G_1(\\mathbb{S})$, the coinduction of the\nnonequivariant sphere spectrum to $G$. The $\\infty$-category of Borel\ncomplete $G$-spectra is then defined as\n$$\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G_{\\textnormal{Borel}} \\mathrel{\\vcenter{\\baselineskip 0.4ex \\lineskiplimit 0pt\n\\hbox{\\scriptsize.}\\hbox{\\scriptsize.}}}%\n=\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G_{A\\textnormal{-cpl}},$$ that is, as complete\nobjects (in the sense of [@mnn17 §2.2]) with respect to the algebra\nobject $A$. This means that a $G$-spectrum is Borel complete if all maps\nit receives from nonequivariantly contractible $G$-spectra are null, as\nfor finite groups.\\\nIn\n[1](#prop:tstructureonlevelwiseborelcomplete){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"prop:tstructureonlevelwiseborelcomplete\"} we observe that\nthere is a right complete t-structure on\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G_{\\textnormal{lwBorel}}$, and for any t-structure\nwe can make sense of the hypercomplete objects as the ones in the right\northogonal of the acyclics. By an acyclic object we mean one for which\nall t-structure homotopy objects vanish. In the main theorem of\n[3](#sec:borelprofinite){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"sec:borelprofinite\"} we then show that\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G_{\\textnormal{Borel}}$ identifies with the full\nsubcategory on the hypercomplete objects with respect to this\nt-structure.\n\n::: thm*\n**Theorem 2**\n([1](#thm:borelandhyperlewelwise){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"thm:borelandhyperlewelwise\"}). *There is a symmetric monoidal\nequivalence\n$$\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G_{\\textnormal{Borel}} \\simeq (\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G_{\\textnormal{lwBorel}})^h.$$*\n:::\n\nIn fact, we work with coefficients in any connective commutative\nnonequivariant ring spectrum, and nonequivariant coefficients are not\nless general than equivariant ones when dealing with Borel complete\ncategories, see [1](#cor:justrestriction){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"cor:justrestriction\"}.\\\nWe then connect the above two versions of Borel complete $G$-spectra for\nprofinite groups $G=\\lim_i \\, G_i$ to $\\infty$-categories of\nrepresentations and étale sheaves. The latter will further down the line\nbe the bridge to étale motives.\n\n::: prop*\n**Proposition 1**\n([1](#prop:sheavesborelcomplete){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"prop:sheavesborelcomplete\"} and\n[1](#prop:sheavesgrmodules){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"prop:sheavesgrmodules\"}). *There is a commutative diagram\nwith horizontal equivalences and fully faithful vertical functors\n$$\\begin{tikzcd}\n    {\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_G}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)_{\\textnormal{Borel}}} & {\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}^{\\wedge}(G\\textsf{\\textup{-set}};R)} & {\\mathcal{D}(\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}(G;R))} \\\\\n    {\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_G}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)_{\\textnormal{lwBorel}}} & {\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}(G\\textsf{\\textup{-set}};R)} & {\\textnormal{colim}_i \\; \\mathcal{D}(\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}(G_i;R)).}\n    \\arrow[\"\\sim\", from=1-1, to=1-2]\n    \\arrow[hook, from=1-1, to=2-1]\n    \\arrow[\"\\sim\", from=1-2, to=1-3]\n    \\arrow[hook, from=1-2, to=2-2]\n    \\arrow[hook, from=1-3, to=2-3]\n    \\arrow[\"\\sim\", from=2-1, to=2-2]\n    \\arrow[\"\\sim\", from=2-2, to=2-3]\n\\end{tikzcd}$$*\n:::\n\nHere $R_G$ is the inflation of a discrete commutative ring $R$ to\n$G$-spectra, the sheaf categories consist of (hyper)sheaves of\n$R$-modules in spectra defined on the site of finite discrete $G$-sets\nwith jointly surjective covering maps,\n$\\mathcal{D}(\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}(G;R))$ denotes the derived\n$\\infty$-category of discrete $(G;R)$-modules, and\n$\\textnormal{colim}_i \\; \\mathcal{D}(\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}(G_i;R))$ is\nthe filtered colimit of the derived categories\n$\\mathcal{D}(\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}(G_i;R))$ with transition maps induced\nby restriction along the quotient maps $G_i \\twoheadrightarrow G_j$,\ntaken in $\\textsf{\\textup{Pr}}^{\\textnormal{L}}$. In fact, for the\nleft-hand square of this diagram the proposition holds for any\nconnective commutative ring spectrum $R$.\\\nBy work of Clausen--Mathew [@cm21 §4.1], both rows agree if the virtual\ncohomological dimension of $G$ is finite, in the case that $R$ is\ndiscrete. Analogous statements can be made for general connective\n$R \\in \\textnormal{CAlg}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$, see\n[1](#prop:sheavesborelcomplete){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"prop:sheavesborelcomplete\"}.\\\nFurthermore, note that for the sheaf categories in the above diagram the\ntwo notions *hypersheaf* and *hypercomplete sheaf* (the latter defined\nwith respect to the canonical t-structure on sheaves) agree. We will\nshow this in\n[1](#prop:hypersheafhypercomplete){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"prop:hypersheafhypercomplete\"} by reducing the case with\ncoefficients in a ring spectrum to the sheaves of spectra case.\\\nWe finally come full circle and note that by Grothendieck's equivalence\n[\\[eq:fetspione\\]](#eq:fetspione){reference-type=\"ref\"\nreference=\"eq:fetspione\"}, étale sheaves on finite étale $S$-schemes are\nthe same as sheaves on finite discrete $G$-sets when $G$ is the étale\nfundamental group $\\pi_1^{\\textnormal{ét}}(S)$. It is then a crucial\n(and well known, see e.g. [@cd16 Proposition 3.1.4]) observation that\nétale sheaves on (finite) étale $S$-schemes already have transfers\n([1](#thm:etaletransfers){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"thm:etaletransfers\"}):\n$$\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\textnormal{ét}}^{(\\wedge)}(\\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}) \\simeq \\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\textnormal{ét}}^{(\\wedge)}(\\textsf{\\textup{Fét}}_S;R).$$\nHere $\\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R)$ is the full subcategory of the\ncategory of smooth schemes with finite correspondences\n$\\textsf{\\textup{SmCor}}(S;R)$ spanned by the finite étale $S$-schemes.\nWe give an independent proof of this result that does not rely on the\nidentifications of hom-sets made in [@cd16]. It is equivariant in\nspirit - morally speaking we can think of étale sheaves as Borel\ncomplete $G$-spectra, since in the finite group case they are right Kan\nextended from the free orbit. They hence have an overlying $G$-spectrum\nwhich canonically admits transfers. For $R$ a discrete commutative ring\nand $G=\\pi_1^{\\textnormal{ét}}(S)$ the full picture then looks as\nfollows:\n\n::: thm*\n**Theorem 3** ([1](#thm:bigdiagram){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"thm:bigdiagram\"}). *There is a commutative diagram of left\nadjoints in which all horizontal functors are equivalences.\n$$\\begin{tikzcd}\n    {\\mathcal{D}\\textsf{\\textup{Perm}}(G;R)} & {\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{\\underline{R}}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)} & {\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\textnormal{Nis}}(\\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})}  \\\\\n    {\\textnormal{colim}_i \\, \\mathcal{D}(\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}(G_i;R))} & {\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_G}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)_{\\textnormal{lwBorel}}} & {\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\textnormal{ét}}(\\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})}  \\\\\n    {\\mathcal{D}(\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}(G;R))} & {\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_G}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)_{\\textnormal{Borel}}} & {\\mathcal{S}\\textnormal{h}_{\\textnormal{ét}}^{\\wedge}(\\textsf{\\textup{FétCor}}(S;R);\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})} \n    \\arrow[\"\\sim\", from=1-1, to=1-2]\n    \\arrow[from=1-1, to=2-1]\n    \\arrow[\"\\sim\", from=1-2, to=1-3]\n    \\arrow[from=1-2, to=2-2]\n    \\arrow[\"\\textsf{\\textup{a}}_{\\textnormal{ét}}\", from=1-3, to=2-3]\n    \\arrow[\"\\sim\", from=2-1, to=2-2]\n    \\arrow[\"L^h\", from=2-1, to=3-1]\n    \\arrow[\"\\sim\", from=2-2, to=2-3]\n    \\arrow[\"L^h\", from=2-2, to=3-2]\n    \\arrow[\"(-)^{\\wedge}_\\textnormal{ét}\", from=2-3, to=3-3]\n    \\arrow[\"\\sim\", from=3-1, to=3-2]\n    \\arrow[\"\\sim\", from=3-2, to=3-3]\n\\end{tikzcd}$$*\n:::\n\nEach of the categories of sheaves with transfers on the right then maps\nto the respective version of smooth Artin motives constructed as a\nlocalising subcategory of effective motives. As stated above, this\nfunctor is always an equivalence in the Nisnevich case\n([1](#thm:damnisasmodunderlr){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"thm:damnisasmodunderlr\"}). In the hypercomplete étale case we\nneed to impose assumptions on base scheme and coefficients to obtain an\nequivalence: If the ring $R$ has positive characteristic $n$ and the\nresidue characteristics of $S$ are prime to $n$, the categories of the\nthird row coincide with $\\mathcal{DAM}_{\\textnormal{ét}}^{\\wedge}(S;R)$,\nas a special form of the rigidity theorem\n([1](#cor:dametassheaves){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"cor:dametassheaves\"}). In the non-hypercomplete étale case an\nanalogous statement would require the computation of certain mapping\nspaces in the corresponding category of effective motives, and we will\nrefrain from doing those.\\\nBy work of Cisinski--Déglise [@cd16 §2] which generalises a theorem of\nVoevodsky [@vsf00 §5, Theorem 4.1.12], all rows as well as the\nrespective categories of Artin motives and effective motives collapse to\na single row when we use coefficients in a $\\mathbb{Q}$-algebra. We\nsummarise this in [1](#thm:bigdiagramright){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"thm:bigdiagramright\"}.\\\n**[Organisation of the paper.]{.upright}** The first two sections are\nentirely devoted to equivariant homotopy theory. In\n[2](#sec:borelfinite){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"sec:borelfinite\"} we review the identification of the Borel\ncomplete subcategory for finite groups as a functor category, as\nestablished by Mathew--Naumann--Noel. We do this with coefficients and\nthen prove basic change of group results.\n[3](#sec:borelprofinite){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"sec:borelprofinite\"} then generalises this theory to\nprofinite groups, where we define the two differing notions alluded to\nabove. The main result of this section is that one is the\nhypercompletion of the other. The latter is then used in\n[4](#sec:sheavesandreps){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"sec:sheavesandreps\"} to connect the Borel complete categories\nof equivariant spectra for profinite groups to categories of étale\nsheaves and representations. In\n[5](#sec:motives){reference-type=\"ref+Label\" reference=\"sec:motives\"} we\ndive into the theory of correspondences and motives, establish an\nidentification of smooth Artin motives for the Nisnevich topology, and\nstudy the effect of étale sheafification in the equivariant and\nrepresentation theoretic setting. We end with Appendix\n[6](#sec:sheaveswithtransfers){reference-type=\"ref\"\nreference=\"sec:sheaveswithtransfers\"} by comparing our definitions of\nmotives with the more classical ones in the literature.\\\n**[Notations and conventions.]{.upright}** We freely use the language of\n$\\infty$-categories as developed by Lurie [@lur09; @lur17; @lur18]. We\nsometimes speak of 'categories' instead of '$\\infty$-categories' when it\nis clear that the context is $\\infty$-categorical. We write\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Spc}}$ for the $\\infty$-category of spaces/homotopy\ntypes and $\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}$ for the $\\infty$-category of spectra.\nThe $G$-equivariant analogues are denoted $\\textsf{\\textup{Spc}}^G$ and\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G$, the latter is what is sometimes referred to as\n'genuine' $G$-spectra. We tacitly identify discrete rings and Mackey\nfunctors with their Eilenberg-MacLane spectra when viewing them as\n(equivariant) spectra. Mapping spaces in an $\\infty$-category\n$\\mathcal{C}$ are denoted $\\textnormal{Map}_{\\mathcal{C}}$, and by\n$\\textnormal{Hom}_{\\mathcal{C}}$ we mean\n$\\pi_0 \\textnormal{Map}_{\\mathcal{C}}$, the hom-set in the homotopy\ncategory $\\textnormal{h}\\mathcal{C}$.\\\n**[Acknowledgements.]{.upright}** I would like to thank my advisor\nMartin Gallauer for his guidance during the work on this project and for\nhis excellent comments on drafts of this paper. I want to thank Timo\nRicharz for suggesting to extend Voevodsky's description of Artin\nmotives to general base schemes. Furthermore, I am indebted to Drew\nHeard, Achim Krause and Marius Nielsen for excellent discussions, many\nhelpful remarks, and for their hospitality during a research visit to\nTrondheim and Oslo. I thank Scott Balchin, David Barnes, Tobias Barthel\nand Luca Pol for comments on an earlier version of this article.\\\nThe author is supported by the Warwick Mathematics Institute Centre for\nDoctoral Training and gratefully acknowledges funding from the\nUniversity of Warwick.",

        "body_markdown": "This section mostly consists of recollections and immediate\ngeneralisations of the results on Borel completeness in [@mnn17]. We\nfirst recall some facts about module $\\infty$-categories and equivariant\nspectra for profinite groups that we will use throughout the paper and\nthen consider Borel completeness for modules over equivariant ring\nspectra in the finite group case. At the end of the section we establish\nchange of group results for Borel complete subcategories.\n\n::: {#rec:modules .rec}\n**Recollection 1**. *If $\\mathcal{C}$ is a presentably symmetric\nmonoidal[^2] stable $\\infty$-category and\n$A \\in \\textnormal{CAlg}(\\mathcal{C})$, then the $\\infty$-category\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_A(\\mathcal{C})$ of $A$-modules in $\\mathcal{C}$\nis presentably symmetric monoidal and stable [@lur17 Theorem 3.4.4.2].\nIt comes with a free-forgetful adjunction\n$$(F_A,U_A): \\mathcal{C}\\rightleftarrows \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_A(\\mathcal{C}),$$\nthe free functor $F_A$ is symmetric monoidal, and the composite $U_AF_A$\nis the functor $(-) \\otimes A: \\mathcal{C}\\to \\mathcal{C}$ [@lur17\nCorollary 4.2.3.7, 4.2.4.8, Theorem 4.5.2.1, §4.5.3]. If $\\mathcal{C}$\nis compactly generated by a set of objects $\\mathcal{G}$, then\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_A(\\mathcal{C})$ is compactly generated by the set\n$F_A(\\mathcal{G})$. If the objects of $\\mathcal{G}$ are also dualisable,\nthen the objects of $F_A(\\mathcal{G})$ are. If the unit of $\\mathcal{C}$\nis compact then $A$ is compact in\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_A(\\mathcal{C})$, so in this case an object of\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_A(\\mathcal{C})$ is compact if and only if it is\ndualisable, and $\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_A(\\mathcal{C})$ is\nrigidly-compactly generated by the set $F_A(\\mathcal{G})$.\\\nA symmetric monoidal functor $\\alpha: \\mathcal{C}\\to \\mathcal{D}$\nrestricts to commutative algebra objects\n$\\textnormal{CAlg}(\\mathcal{C}) \\to \\textnormal{CAlg}(\\mathcal{D})$, and\nfor any $A \\in \\textnormal{CAlg}(\\mathcal{C})$ there is an induced\nsymmetric monoidal functor\n$$\\bar{\\alpha}: \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_A(\\mathcal{C}) \\to \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{\\alpha(A)}(\\mathcal{D})$$\non module categories. If $\\alpha$ preserves colimits then so does the\ninduced $\\bar{\\alpha}$ [@lur17 Corollary 4.2.3.5], and as explained in\n[@erg22 Remark 1.1.11] both squares in the following diagram commute.\n$$\\begin{tikzcd}\n    \\mathcal{C}& \\mathcal{D}\\\\\n    {\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_A(\\mathcal{C})} & {\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{\\alpha(A)}(\\mathcal{D})}\n    \\arrow[\"\\alpha\", from=1-1, to=1-2]\n    \\arrow[\"\"{name=0, anchor=center, inner sep=0}, \"{F_A}\"', shift right=2, from=1-1, to=2-1]\n    \\arrow[\"\"{name=1, anchor=center, inner sep=0}, \"{F_{\\alpha(A)}}\"', shift right=2, from=1-2, to=2-2]\n    \\arrow[\"\"{name=2, anchor=center, inner sep=0}, \"{U_A}\"', shift right=2, from=2-1, to=1-1]\n    \\arrow[\"\\bar{\\alpha}\", from=2-1, to=2-2]\n    \\arrow[\"\"{name=3, anchor=center, inner sep=0}, \"{U_{\\alpha(A)}}\"', shift right=2, from=2-2, to=1-2]\n    \\arrow[\"\\dashv\"{anchor=center}, draw=none, from=0, to=2]\n    \\arrow[\"\\dashv\"{anchor=center}, draw=none, from=1, to=3]\n\\end{tikzcd}$$ If $\\alpha$ preserves limits, then so does $\\bar{\\alpha}$\n[@lur17 Corollary 4.2.3.3], and a right adjoint\n$\\beta: \\mathcal{D}\\to \\mathcal{C}$ to $\\alpha$ induces a right adjoint\n$\\bar{\\beta}: \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{\\alpha(A)}(\\mathcal{D}) \\to \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_A(\\mathcal{C})$\nto the functor\n$\\bar{\\alpha}: \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_A(\\mathcal{C}) \\to \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{\\alpha(A)}(\\mathcal{D})$.\nAs a right adjoint to a symmetric monoidal functor the functor\n$\\beta: \\mathcal{D}\\to \\mathcal{C}$ is lax symmetric monoidal, and when\n$B \\in \\textnormal{CAlg}(\\mathcal{D}^{\\otimes})$, then we also have an\ninduced lax symmetric monoidal functor\n$$\\tilde{\\beta}: \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_B(\\mathcal{D}) \\to \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{\\beta(B)}(\\mathcal{C}).$$\nIt factors as\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_B(\\mathcal{D}) \\stackrel{\\varepsilon_B^*}{\\longrightarrow} \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{\\alpha \\beta(B)}(\\mathcal{D}) \\stackrel{\\bar{\\beta}}{\\longrightarrow} \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{\\beta(B)}(\\mathcal{C})$,\nwhere $\\varepsilon_B^*$ is the restriction of scalars along the counit\n$\\varepsilon_B: \\alpha \\beta(B) \\to B$, and hence $\\tilde{\\beta}$ has a\nsymmetric monoidal left adjoint\n$\\tilde{\\alpha}: \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{\\beta(B)}(\\mathcal{C}) \\to \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_B(\\mathcal{D})$\ngiven by the composition\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{\\beta(B)}(\\mathcal{C}) \\stackrel{\\bar{\\alpha}}{\\longrightarrow} \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{\\alpha \\beta(B)}(\\mathcal{D}) \\stackrel{\\varepsilon_{B,!}}{\\longrightarrow} \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_B(\\mathcal{D})$,\nwhere $\\varepsilon_{B,!}$ is the extension of scalars along\n$\\varepsilon_B: \\alpha \\beta(B) \\to B$.*\n:::\n\nThere are multiple models for the $\\infty$-category of $G$-spectra\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G$ for a profinite group $G$ which are all known\nto be equivalent [@bbb24 §A]. Our preferred model in this paper will be\nthe one of spectral Mackey functors [@bar17; @bgs20], since in this\nmodel the relation to the Borel complete subcategory is particularly\nclear. We could hence take the functor category\n$$\\textnormal{Fun}^{\\times}(\\textsf{\\textup{Span}}(G)^{\\textnormal{op}},\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$$\nas a definition for $\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G$. Here\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Span}}(G)$ denotes the effective Burnside\n$\\infty$-category of finite continuous $G$-sets [@bar17 §3, Example B]\nand the superscript $\\times$ indicates that we are taking the full\nsubcategory of finite product preserving functors.[^3]\n\n::: rec\n**Recollection 1**. *The *$\\infty$-category of $G$-spectra*\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G$ for a profinite group $G$ is stable and\npresentably symmetric monoidal. We denote the symmetric monoidal product\nby $\\otimes$ and the internal mapping $G$-spectrum by\n$\\underline{\\textnormal{map}}_{\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G}(-,-)$. It\nreceives a symmetric monoidal left adjoint suspension functor\n$\\Sigma^{\\infty}: \\textsf{\\textup{Spc}}^G_{\\ast}\\to \\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G$\nfrom pointed $G$-spaces. We write\n$\\Sigma^{\\infty}_+: \\textsf{\\textup{Spc}}^G\\to \\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G$\nfor the composition $\\Sigma^{\\infty} \\circ (-)_+$, where the functor\n$(-)_+: \\textsf{\\textup{Spc}}^G\\to \\textsf{\\textup{Spc}}^G_{\\ast}$ adds\na disjoint base point with trivial action.\\\nThe sphere spectrum $\\Sigma^{\\infty}_+ G/G$ is denoted\n$\\mathbb{S}_G = \\mathbb{S}^0_G$. It is the unit of the symmetric\nmonoidal structure. The $\\infty$-category $\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G$ is\nrigidly compactly generated by the suspension spectra of orbits\n$\\Sigma^{\\infty}_+G/H$, for open subgroups $H \\leq G$. It has a natural\nt-structure for which the t-structure homotopy objects agree with the\nhomotopy Mackey functors\n$\\pi_n^{H}(-) = \\textnormal{Hom}_{\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G}(\\Sigma^{\\infty + n}_+ G/H,-)$.\nThis t-structure is both left and right complete, compatible with\nfiltered colimits, and it is compatible with the symmetric monoidal\nstructure on $\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G$, in the sense that\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G_{\\geq 0}$ is a symmetric monoidal subcategory.*\n:::\n\n::: rec\n**Recollection 1**. *For any homomorphism of profinite groups (i.e.,\ncontinuous group homomorphism) $\\varphi: G \\to G'$ there is a symmetric\nmonoidal left adjoint functor\n$\\varphi^*: \\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^{G'} \\to \\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G$ with\nlax symmetric monoidal right adjoint\n$\\varphi_*: \\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^{G} \\to \\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^{G'}$.\\\nIf $\\varphi$ is the inclusion of a closed subgroup\n$H \\hookrightarrow G$, the left adjoint\n$\\varphi^*: \\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^{G} \\to \\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^{H}$ is\nthe *restriction functor* $\\textnormal{res}^G_H$, and its right\nadjoint[^4] is the *coinduction functor* $\\textnormal{coind}^G_H$. If\n$\\varphi: G \\twoheadrightarrow G/N$ is a quotient homomorphism for\n$N \\trianglelefteq G$ a closed normal subgroup then\n$\\varphi^*: \\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^{G/N} \\to \\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^{G}$ is\nthe *inflation functor* $\\textnormal{infl}^G_{G/N}$, and its right\nadjoint $\\varphi_*$ is the *categorical fixed point functor*\n$(-)^N: \\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^{G} \\to \\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^{G/N}$.*\n:::\n\nWe explain what the above functors mean in terms of spectral Mackey\nfunctors.\n\n::: {#rem:changeofgroupspectralmackey .rem}\n**Remark 1**. *For a closed subgroup $H\\leq G$ the functor\n$\\overline{\\textnormal{res}}^G_H: \\textsf{\\textup{Span}}(G) \\to \\textsf{\\textup{Span}}(H)$\nthat restricts the $G$-action to an $H$-action induces the adjunction\n$(\\textnormal{res}^G_H,\\textnormal{coind}^G_H)$ through restriction and\nleft Kan extension\n$$((\\overline{\\textnormal{res}}^G_H)_!,(\\overline{\\textnormal{res}}^G_H)^*): \\textnormal{Fun}^{\\times}(\\textsf{\\textup{Span}}(G)^{\\textnormal{op}},\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}) \\rightleftarrows \\textnormal{Fun}^{\\times}(\\textsf{\\textup{Span}}(H)^{\\textnormal{op}},\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}).$$\nWhen $H$ additionally is of finite index (i.e., open) the functor\n$\\overline{\\textnormal{res}}^G_H$ has a left adjoint\n$\\overline{\\textnormal{ind}}^G_H: \\textsf{\\textup{Span}}(H) \\to \\textsf{\\textup{Span}}(G), \\; X \\mapsto (G \\times X)/H,$\nwhere $H$ acts by $h(g,x)=(gh^{-1},hx)$. For the induced adjunction\n$$((\\overline{\\textnormal{ind}}^G_H)_!,(\\overline{\\textnormal{ind}}^G_H)^*): \\textnormal{Fun}^{\\times}(\\textsf{\\textup{Span}}(H)^{\\textnormal{op}},\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}) \\rightleftarrows \\textnormal{Fun}^{\\times}(\\textsf{\\textup{Span}}(G)^{\\textnormal{op}},\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$$\nwe thus have\n$(\\overline{\\textnormal{ind}}^G_H)^* \\simeq (\\overline{\\textnormal{res}}^G_H)_! \\simeq \\textnormal{res}^G_H$\nand its left adjoint $(\\overline{\\textnormal{ind}}^G_H)_!$ is usually\nreferred to as the *induction functor* $\\textnormal{ind}^G_H$. It is\nequivalent to $\\textnormal{coind}^G_H$ via the Wirthmüller isomorphism,\nsee [@nar17 §A.3], [@cmnn24 §A].\\\nAnalogously, when $N \\trianglelefteq G$ is a closed normal subgroup\nthere is a functor on span categories\n$\\overline{\\textnormal{infl}}^G_{G/N}: \\textsf{\\textup{Span}}(G/N) \\to \\textsf{\\textup{Span}}(G), \\; (G/N)/(H/N) \\mapsto G/H$.\nIt induces\n$$((\\overline{\\textnormal{infl}}^G_{G/N})_!,(\\overline{\\textnormal{infl}}^G_{G/N})^*): \\textnormal{Fun}^{\\times}(\\textsf{\\textup{Span}}(G/N)^{\\textnormal{op}},\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}) \\rightleftarrows \\textnormal{Fun}^{\\times}(\\textsf{\\textup{Span}}(G)^{\\textnormal{op}},\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}),$$\nwhich recovers the adjunction $(\\textnormal{infl}^G_{G/N},(-)^N)$, see\n[@bar17 Example B].*\n:::\n\nLet us now fix a finite group $G$ and a commutative equivariant ring\nspectrum $R \\in \\textnormal{CAlg}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)$. We will\nreturn to the profinite case in the next section.\n\n::: {#rec:coinddual .rec}\n**Recollection 1**. *Since any finite $G$-set $T$ is a commutative\ncoalgebra in $\\textsf{\\textup{Spc}}^G$, the internal mapping spectrum\n$\\mathbb{D}(T) \\mathrel{\\vcenter{\\baselineskip 0.4ex \\lineskiplimit 0pt\n\\hbox{\\scriptsize.}\\hbox{\\scriptsize.}}}%\n=\\underline{\\textnormal{map}}_{\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G}(\\Sigma^{\\infty}_+T, \\mathbb{S}_G)$\nhas the structure of a commutative algebra object in\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G$. By [@bchnl25 Lemma 3.8] there is an\nequivalence\n$$\\mathbb{D}(G/H) \\otimes R \\stackrel{\\sim}{\\longrightarrow} \\textnormal{coind}^G_H\\textnormal{res}^G_H(R)$$\nin $\\textnormal{CAlg}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)$ which is adjoint to the\nmap\n$\\textnormal{res}^G_H(\\mathbb{D}(G/H) \\otimes R )\\to \\textnormal{res}^G_H(R)$\nthat is obtained from the projection\n$\\textnormal{res}^G_H(\\mathbb{D}(G/H)) \\to \\mathbb{S}_H$ by base change.\nAs $\\mathbb{D}(G/H) \\otimes R$ is the image of $\\mathbb{D}(G/H)$ under\nthe free functor\n$F_R: \\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G\\to \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_R(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)$,\nwe can view $\\mathbb{D}(G/H) \\otimes R$ as a commutative algebra object\nof $\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_R(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)$.*\n:::\n\n::: rem\n**Remark 1**. *Since $\\mathbb{D}(G/H) \\otimes R$ is a dualisable\n$R$-module with dual $\\Sigma^{\\infty}_+G/H \\otimes R$ there is an\nequivalence of $R$-modules\n$\\mathbb{D}(G/H) \\otimes R \\simeq \\underline{\\textnormal{map}}_{\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_R(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)}(\\Sigma^{\\infty}_+G/H \\otimes R, R)$,\nand the underlying $G$-spectrum of this is\n$\\underline{\\textnormal{map}}_{\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G}(\\Sigma^{\\infty}_+G/H, R)$.*\n:::\n\nThe definition for completeness with respect to an algebra object $A$ we\nwill use in this paper is the one of [@mnn17 §2.2]. When $A$ is\ndualisable, [@mnn17 Proposition 3.11] shows that it agrees with the\nperhaps more common one that defines complete objects as the twofold\nright orthogonal of torsion objects (which are the objects in the\nlocalising tensor ideal generated by $A$). The dualisability assumption\nholds in the finite group case.\n\n::: {#defi:borelcomplete .defi}\n**Definition 1**. *An $R$-module\n$X \\in \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_R(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)$ is *Borel\ncomplete* if it is complete with respect to the algebra object\n$\\mathbb{D}(G) \\otimes R$. That is, for all\n$Y \\in \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_R(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)$ with\n$Y \\otimes_R (\\mathbb{D}(G) \\otimes R) \\simeq 0$ the mapping space\n$\\textnormal{Map}_{\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_R(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)}(Y,X)$\nis contractible. We write\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_R(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)_{\\textnormal{Borel}} \\subseteq \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_R(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)$\nfor the full subcategory on the Borel complete $R$-modules.*\n:::\n\n::: {#rem:borelcompleteforget .rem}\n**Remark 1**. *The case $R=\\mathbb{S}_G$ is the now classical notion of\nBorel completeness for $G$-spectra [@mnn17 §6.3]. By [@mnn17 §2.2] the\nsubcategory\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_R(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)_{\\textnormal{Borel}}$\nis presentable and the inclusion\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_R(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)_{\\textnormal{Borel}} \\hookrightarrow \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_R(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)$\nhas a left adjoint $L_{G;R}$ called *Borel completion*. There is a\nunique symmetric monoidal structure on\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_R(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)_{\\textnormal{Borel}}$\nthat makes $L_{G;R}$ into a symmetric monoidal functor.*\n:::\n\n::: {#rem:tensorcondition .rem}\n**Remark 1**. *Since the forgetful functor $U_R$ is conservative and the\nfree-forgetful adjunction satisfies a projection formula the condition\n$Y \\otimes_R (\\mathbb{D}(G) \\otimes R) \\simeq 0$ is equivalent to\n$U_R(Y) \\otimes \\mathbb{D}(G) \\simeq 0$.*\n:::\n\n::: {#rem:completeunderlyingeasydirection .rem}\n**Remark 1**. *If a module\n$X \\in \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_R(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)$ is Borel\ncomplete, then the underlying $G$-spectrum\n$U_R(X) \\in \\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G$ is Borel complete. Indeed, assume\nthat $Y \\in \\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G$ satisfies\n$Y \\otimes \\mathbb{D}(G) \\simeq 0$, then\n$F_R(Y) \\otimes_R (\\mathbb{D}(G) \\otimes R) \\simeq F_R(Y \\otimes \\mathbb{D}(G)) \\simeq 0$\nand hence we have that\n$\\textnormal{Map}_{\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G}(Y,U_R(X)) \\simeq \\textnormal{Map}_{\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_R(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)}(F_R(Y),X) \\simeq 0$.\\\nSimilarly, when $X \\in \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_R(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)$\nis Borel complete, $U_R(X) \\in \\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G$ is complete with\nrespect to the algebra object\n$\\mathbb{D}(G) \\otimes R \\in \\textnormal{CAlg}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)$.\nWe will show the converse to the first statement in\n[1](#cor:completionunderlying){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"cor:completionunderlying\"}.*\n:::\n\nAs in the case without coefficients, we can give an explicit description\nof the Borel completion as a functor\n$L_{G;R}: \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_R(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G) \\to \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_R(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)_{\\textnormal{Borel}} \\hookrightarrow \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_R(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)$.\n\n::: {#lem:completionexplicit .lem}\n**Lemma 1**. *Let\n$X \\in \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_R(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)$. The map\n$X \\to \\underline{\\textnormal{map}}_{\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_R(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)}(\\Sigma^{\\infty}_+EG \\otimes R, X)$\nexhibits the target as the Borel completion of $X$.*\n:::\n\n::: proof\n*Proof.* By [@mnn17 Proposition 2.21] the completion $L_{G;R}(X)$ is\ncomputed as\n$\\textnormal{Tot}(X \\otimes_R \\textnormal{CB}^{\\bullet}(\\mathbb{D}(G) \\otimes R))$,\nthe totalisation of the cobar construction of $\\mathbb{D}(G) \\otimes R$\ntensored with $X$. We now note that there are equivalences\n$$\\begin{align*}\nX \\otimes_R (\\mathbb{D}(G) \\otimes R)^{\\otimes_R \\bullet} &\\simeq X \\otimes_R (\\underline{\\textnormal{map}}_{\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_R(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)}(\\Sigma^{\\infty}_+G^{\\bullet}, \\mathbb{S}_G) \\otimes R) \\\\\n&\\simeq X \\otimes_R \\underline{\\textnormal{map}}_{\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_R(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)}(\\Sigma^{\\infty}_+G^{\\bullet} \\otimes R, R) \\\\\n&\\simeq \\underline{\\textnormal{map}}_{\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_R(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)}(\\Sigma^{\\infty}_+G^{\\bullet} \\otimes R, X).\n\\end{align*}$$ Totalising gives\n$\\underline{\\textnormal{map}}_{\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_R(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)}(\\Sigma^{\\infty}_+EG \\otimes R, X)$,\nusing the standard simplicial decomposition of the free contractible\n$G$-space $EG$ as in [@mnn17 Proposition 6.6]. ◻\n:::\n\n::: {#cor:completionunderlying .cor}\n**Corollary 1**. *A module\n$X \\in \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_R(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)$ is Borel\ncomplete if and only if the underlying $G$-spectrum $U_R(X)$ is.*\n:::\n\n::: proof\n*Proof.* By [1](#lem:completionexplicit){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"lem:completionexplicit\"} $X$ is Borel complete if and only if\nthe completion map\n$$X \\to \\underline{\\textnormal{map}}_{\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_R(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)}(\\Sigma^{\\infty}_+EG \\otimes R, X)$$\nis an equivalence. Since $U_R$ is conservative, this happens if and only\nif the map\n$$U_R(X) \\to U_R(\\underline{\\textnormal{map}}_{\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_R(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)}(\\Sigma^{\\infty}_+EG \\otimes R, X)) \\simeq \\underline{\\textnormal{map}}_{\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G}(\\Sigma^{\\infty}_+EG, U_R(X))$$\nis an equivalence. But this is precisely the completion map for\n$U_R(X)$. ◻\n:::\n\nRecall from [@mnn17 Proposition 6.17] that the $\\infty$-category of\nBorel complete $G$-spectra has a particularly simple description as\nspectra with a $G$-action. We can generalise this to the situation with\ncoefficients.\n\n::: {#lem:resasbasechange .lem}\n**Lemma 1**. *There is a symmetric monoidal equivalence\n$$\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{\\mathbb{D}(G)\\otimes R}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G) \\stackrel{\\sim}{\\longrightarrow} \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{\\textnormal{res}^G_1(R)}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}),$$\nand the equivalence functor fits into the following commutative diagram:\n$$\\begin{tikzcd}\n    {\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)} & \\\\\n    {\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{\\textnormal{res}^G_1(R)}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})} & {\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{\\mathbb{D}(G)\\otimes R}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)}\n    \\arrow[\"{\\textnormal{res}^G_1}\"', from=1-1, to=2-1]\n    \\arrow[\"{F_{\\mathbb{D}(G) \\otimes R}}\", from=1-1, to=2-2]\n    \\arrow[\"\\sim\"', from=2-2, to=2-1]\n\\end{tikzcd}$$*\n:::\n\n::: proof\n*Proof.* The case for $R = \\mathbb{S}$ is [@mnn17 Theorem 5.32] (see\nalso [@bds15 Theorem 1.1] for the original version), and a more general\nstatement than the one above is shown in [@bchnl25 Proposition 3.9]. ◻\n:::\n\n::: {#rem:nonequivariantlycontractible .rem}\n**Remark 1**. *When $R = \\mathbb{S}_G$,\n[1](#lem:resasbasechange){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"lem:resasbasechange\"} shows that for a $G$-spectrum $Y$ the\ncondition $Y \\otimes \\mathbb{D}(G) \\simeq 0$ is equivalent to $Y$ being\n*nonequivariantly contractible* (that is,\n$\\textnormal{res}^G_1(Y) \\simeq 0$) [@mnn17 Proposition 6.15]. Since\n$\\mathbb{D}(G)$ is dualisable these conditions also agree with the one\nthat $Y$ is *$\\mathbb{D}(G)^{-1}$-local* [@mnn17 §3.2].\\\nMore generally, if $Y$ is an $R$-module we have\n$Y \\otimes_R (\\mathbb{D}(G) \\otimes R) \\simeq 0$ if and only if\n$\\textnormal{res}^G_1(Y) \\simeq 0$ in\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{\\textnormal{res}^G_1(R)}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$,\nwhich holds if and only if\n$\\textnormal{res}^G_1(U_R(Y)) \\simeq U_R(\\textnormal{res}^G_1(Y)) \\simeq 0$\nin $\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}$.*\n:::\n\n::: {#prop:borelcompleteasfun .prop}\n**Proposition 1**. *There is an equivalence of symmetric monoidal\n$\\infty$-categories\n$$\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_R(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)_{\\textnormal{Borel}} \\simeq \\textnormal{Fun}(BG,\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{\\textnormal{res}^G_1(R)}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})),$$\nwhere the right-hand side carries the pointwise monoidal structure.*\n:::\n\n::: proof\n*Proof.* This is the same proof as in [@mnn17 Proposition 6.17], where\nthe statement is shown for $R = \\mathbb{S}_G$. We note that\n$\\mathbb{D}(G) \\otimes R$ is a dualisable object of\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_R(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)$ since it is the image\nof the dualisable object $\\mathbb{D}(G)$ under the free functor. Hence\nby [@mnn17 Theorem 2.30] the $\\infty$-category of\n$(\\mathbb{D}(G) \\otimes R)$-complete objects is computed as the\ntotalisation of the cosimplicial extension of scalars diagram\n$$\\begin{equation}\n\\label{diag:totalisation}\n\\begin{tikzcd}\n    {\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{\\mathbb{D}(G)\\otimes R}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)} & {\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{\\mathbb{D}(G \\times G) \\otimes R}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)} & {\\cdots}\n    \\arrow[shift right=2, from=1-1, to=1-2]\n    \\arrow[shift left=2, from=1-1, to=1-2]\n    \\arrow[from=1-2, to=1-1]\n    \\arrow[from=1-2, to=1-3]\n    \\arrow[shift left=4, from=1-2, to=1-3]\n    \\arrow[shift right=4, from=1-2, to=1-3]\n    \\arrow[shift right=2, from=1-3, to=1-2]\n    \\arrow[shift left=2, from=1-3, to=1-2]\n\\end{tikzcd}\n\\end{equation}$$ which is obtained by applying the module functor to the\ncobar construction for the algebra object\n$\\mathbb{D}(G) \\otimes R \\in \\textnormal{CAlg}(\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_R(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G))$.\nBy [1](#lem:resasbasechange){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"lem:resasbasechange\"} we can identify\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{\\mathbb{D}(G)\\otimes R}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)$\nwith\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{\\textnormal{res}^G_1(R)}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$,\nand right=2, from=1-1, to=1-2]\n    \\arrow[shift left=2, from=1-1, to=1-2]\n    \\arrow[from=1-2, to=1-1]\n    \\arrow[from=1-2, to=1-3]\n    \\arrow[shift left=4, from=1-2, to=1-3]\n    \\arrow[shift category\n$\\textnormal{Fun}(BG,\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{\\textnormal{res}^G_1(R)}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}))$,\nusing the standard bar construction simplicial diagram that realises to\n$BG$. ◻\n:::\n\n::: {#rem:forgetfulonborelcompletes .rem}\n**Remark 1**. *The observation made in\n[1](#rem:borelcompleteforget){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"rem:borelcompleteforget\"} says that the forgetful functor\n$U_R: \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_R(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G) \\to \\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G$\ninduces a functor\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_R(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)_{\\textnormal{Borel}} \\to \\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G_{\\textnormal{Borel}}$,\nwhich we can equivalently describe as the postcomposition\n$$\\textnormal{Fun}(BG,\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{\\textnormal{res}^G_1(R)}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})) \\to \\textnormal{Fun}(BG,\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$$\nwith the forgetful functor\n$U_{\\textnormal{res}^G_1(R)}: \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{\\textnormal{res}^G_1(R)}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}) \\to \\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}$.*\n:::\n\nIn particular, we see that the Borel complete subcategory of\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_R(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)$ only depends on the\nunderlying nonequivariant spectrum $\\textnormal{res}^G_1(R)$ of $R$. We\ncan make this precise as follows.\n\n::: {#cor:justrestriction .cor}\n**Corollary 1**. *There is an equivalence of symmetric monoidal\n$\\infty$-categories\n$$\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_R(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)_{\\textnormal{Borel}} \\simeq \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{\\textnormal{infl}^G_{G/G}\\textnormal{res}^G_1(R)}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)_{\\textnormal{Borel}}.$$*\n:::\n\n::: proof\n*Proof.* Since\n$\\textnormal{res}^G_1\\textnormal{infl}^G_{G/G} \\simeq \\textnormal{id}$\nas symmetric monoidal functors\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}\\to \\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}$ there is an equivalence\nof algebra objects\n$\\textnormal{res}^G_1(R) \\simeq \\textnormal{res}^G_1\\textnormal{infl}^G_1\\textnormal{res}^G_1(R)$.\nThe statement then follows from\n[1](#prop:borelcompleteasfun){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"prop:borelcompleteasfun\"}. ◻\n:::\n\n::: {#ex:manylambdas .ex}\n**Example 1**. *For $\\Lambda$ a discrete commutative ring, we can\nconsider the Eilenberg-MacLane spectrum associated to its constant\nMackey functor $\\underline{\\Lambda}$, the Eilenberg-MacLane spectrum\nassociated to the $\\Lambda$-linear Burnside Mackey functor\n$\\mathbb{A}_{\\Lambda}$, and the inflation $\\Lambda_G$ of its\nnonequivariant Eilenberg-MacLane spectrum to $\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G$.\nThen all of the three Borel complete categories associated to these\nequivariant ring spectra are equivalent to\n$\\textnormal{Fun}(BG,\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{\\Lambda}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}))$.*\n:::\n\nWe will hence restrict our study of the Borel complete category with\ncoefficients to coefficients of the from\n$R_G \\mathrel{\\vcenter{\\baselineskip 0.4ex \\lineskiplimit 0pt\n\\hbox{\\scriptsize.}\\hbox{\\scriptsize.}}}%\n=\\textnormal{infl}^G_{G/G}(R)$, where\n$R \\in \\textnormal{CAlg}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$ is a nonequivariant ring\nspectrum. Note that this of course includes the case\n$R_G = \\mathbb{S}_G$.\n\n::: rem\n**Remark 1**. *Consider the adjunction\n$(L_{G;\\mathbb{S}_G},\\iota): \\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G\\rightleftarrows \\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G_{\\textnormal{Borel}}$.\nIn view of [1](#prop:borelcompleteasfun){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"prop:borelcompleteasfun\"} we can express it in terms of\nspectral Mackey functors as\n$$(\\theta^*,\\theta_*): \\textnormal{Fun}^{\\times}(\\textsf{\\textup{Span}}(G)^{\\textnormal{op}},\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}) \\rightleftarrows \\textnormal{Fun}(BG,\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}),$$\nwhere $\\theta^*$ restricts along the map\n$\\theta: BG \\to \\textsf{\\textup{Span}}(G)^{\\textnormal{op}}$ that picks\nout the orbit $G/1$, hence $\\theta^*(X)$ is given by the mapping\nspectrum\n$\\textnormal{map}_{\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G}(\\Sigma^\\infty_+G/1,X)$, and\nthe functor $\\theta_*$ is given by right Kan extension [@bgs20 §8]. One\nmay also view the functor $\\theta^*$ as the one that the restriction\n$\\textnormal{res}^G_1: \\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G\\to \\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}$\nfactors through by remembering the $G$-action on the section of the\norbit $G/1$.\\\nThe functor $\\theta_!$ given by left Kan extension is fully faithful as\nwell and has essential image the $G$-spectra with geometric fixed points\nconcentrated at the trivial group [@hau24 §2]. By [@psw22 §4] for\n$R=\\mathbb{Z}$ and [@bhs23 §14] for the general case there is a\nsymmetric monoidal equivalence\n$$\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_G}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G) \\simeq \\textnormal{Fun}^{\\times}(\\textsf{\\textup{Span}}(G)^{\\textnormal{op}},\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_R(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})),$$\nand we can express the adjunction\n$(L_{G;R},\\iota): \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_G}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G) \\rightleftarrows \\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_G}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)_{\\textnormal{Borel}}$\nas one of functor categories\n$$(\\theta^*,\\theta_*): \\textnormal{Fun}^{\\times}(\\textsf{\\textup{Span}}(G)^{\\textnormal{op}},\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_R(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})) \\rightleftarrows \\textnormal{Fun}(BG,\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_R(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})),$$\nwhere the functor\n$\\theta: BG \\to \\textsf{\\textup{Span}}(G)^{\\textnormal{op}}$ is as\nbefore. Now $\\theta^*$ can be expressed as the mapping $R$-module\nspectrum\n$\\textnormal{map}_{\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_R(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)}(\\Sigma^\\infty_+G,-)$.\nIn view of\n[1](#rem:forgetfulonborelcompletes){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"rem:forgetfulonborelcompletes\"} there is a diagram\n$$\\begin{tikzcd}\n    {\\textnormal{Fun}^{\\times}(\\textsf{\\textup{Span}}(G)^{\\textnormal{op}},\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_R(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}))} & {\\textnormal{Fun}^{\\times}(\\textsf{\\textup{Span}}(G)^{\\textnormal{op}},\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})} \\\\\n    {\\textnormal{Fun}(BG,\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_R(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}))} & {\\textnormal{Fun}(BG,\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})}\n    \\arrow[\"{U_R}\", from=1-1, to=1-2]\n    \\arrow[\"\"{name=0, anchor=center, inner sep=0}, \"{\\theta^*}\"', shift right=2, from=1-1, to=2-1]\n    \\arrow[\"\"{name=1, anchor=center, inner sep=0}, \"{\\theta^*}\"', shift right=2, from=1-2, to=2-2]\n    \\arrow[\"\"{name=2, anchor=center, inner sep=0}, \"{\\theta_*}\"', shift right=2, hook, from=2-1, to=1-1]\n    \\arrow[\"{U_R}\", from=2-1, to=2-2]\n    \\arrow[\"\"{name=3, anchor=center, inner sep=0}, \"{\\theta_*}\"', shift right=2, hook, from=2-2, to=1-2]\n    \\arrow[\"\\dashv\"{anchor=center}, draw=none, from=0, to=2]\n    \\arrow[\"\\dashv\"{anchor=center}, draw=none, from=1, to=3]\n\\end{tikzcd}$$ in which both squares commute. The horizontal functors\npostcompose with the forgetful functor\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}) \\to \\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}$.\n[1](#cor:completionunderlying){reference-type=\"ref+Label\"\nreference=\"cor:completionunderlying\"} says that $X$ in the top left is\nin the essential image of $\\theta_*$ if and only if $U_R(X)$ is in the\nessential image of $\\theta_*$.*\n:::\n\n::: {#cor:tstructureonborelcomplete .cor}\n**Corollary 1**. *When the coefficients $R$ are connective, there is a\nt-structure on\n$\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_{R_G}(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}^G)_{\\textnormal{Borel}}$\nwhich makes the localisation functor $L_{G;R}$ t-exact. The heart is\ngiven by the category $\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}(G;\\pi_0(R))$ of\n$\\pi_0(R)$-modules with a linear $G$-action.*\n:::\n\n::: proof\n*Proof.* First note that $\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_R(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}})$\nhas a t-structure which is detected on the level of underlying spectra\n[@lur17 Proposition 7.1.1.13]. Then the functor category\n$\\textnormal{Fun}(BG,\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_R(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}))$\ninherits a t-structure which is detected pointwise. Similarly, the\nt-structure on\n$\\textnormal{Fun}^{\\times}(\\textsf{\\textup{Span}}(G)^{\\textnormal{op}},\\textsf{\\textup{Mod}}_R(\\textsf{\\textup{Sp}}))$\nis detected pointwise after forgetting the $R$-module structure [@bgs20\n§6]. It follows that the restriction functor $\\theta^*$ is t-exact.
